articles.title: Rupee falls 11 paise to 96.36 against US dollar during early trade
articles.description: The rupee depreciated 11 paise to 96.36 against the US dollar in early trade on Wednesday as crude oil prices climbed on renewed geopolitical tensions, and demand for the US dollar increased as investors moved toward safe-haven assets. Forex traders said concerns over the security of oil shipments through the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz continue to support crude oil prices. Moreover, Houthi threats against shipping and ongoing US-Iran hostilities have kept a geopolitical risk premium in the market, they said. At the interbank foreign exchange market the rupee opened at 96.36, registering a fall of 11 paise from its previous close. On Tuesday, the rupee had settled at 96.25 against the American currency. Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was trading at 101.15 down 0.01 per cent, as the latest escalation in the US-Iran conflict has increased demand for the US dollar as a safe-haven currency. articles.title: Pakistan seeks $10 billion US stabilization facility to shore up reserves
articles.description: Pakistan has requested a ten billion dollar exchange stabilization facility from the United States. This loan aims to bolster foreign exchange reserves and ease pressure on the Pakistani rupee. The request follows Pakistan's diplomatic efforts in brokering talks over the Iran war. This facility would reduce reliance on multilateral financing and IMF programs. It also seeks to deepen bilateral economic cooperation and attract U.S. investment.

articles.title: Sebi directs depositories to freeze promoter holdings during buyback period, new rules explained
articles.description: Sebi has directed depositories to freeze promoter holdings during company buyback periods. This restriction will be in effect from board approval until the offer closes. Promoters can still participate in buybacks through the tender offer route. Existing pledges created before the buyback period can also be invoked. Depositories must implement these operational systems by August 1.

articles.title: India ran a $4-trillion economy half-blind for decades. That just ended
articles.description: For decades, India has tracked factory, mining, and electricity output every month through the Index of Industrial Production, even though services account for more than half of the economy. That gap has finally begun to close. The government has released monthly production indices for 19 service industries, using GST returns and regulatory data to estimate changes in real output. This could transform GDP forecasting, monetary-policy analysis, and investment research. But it is still only a trial series.
